description: We're Team Eternal, working on the Space Mission Design Game challenge for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our goal is to create an engaging, educational game where players design space missions, explore mission scenarios, and make strategic decisions. We're looking for passionate collaborators interested in coding, game development, UI/UX design, animation, AI, and space science. Beginners with enthusiasm and a willingness to learn are welcome!
summary: ORBITFORGE is an interactive space mission design simulator developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. It allows users to experience spacecraft engineering by designing exploration missions to the Moon and Mars. Players select scientific objectives, configure spacecraft systems, manage mass, power generation, energy consumption, and budget, and test their designs through mission simulations. The platform features interactive 3D spacecraft visualization and NASA-referenced scientific instruments and mission information. By combining scientific exploration with engineering trade-offs and interactive gameplay, ORBITFORGE makes the complexities of real space mission planning more accessible and engaging for students and space enthusiasts.
details:
ORBITFORGE is an interactive space mission design simulator that transforms spacecraft engineering and planetary exploration into an educational gameplay experience. Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, it focuses on designing spacecraft capable of completing scientific exploration missions to the Moon and Mars.

Users can select a planetary mission, explore its scientific objectives, and configure a spacecraft using different engineering systems, including the spacecraft bus, scientific instruments, propulsion, power generation, and communications.

The simulation evaluates spacecraft configurations against engineering constraints such as total mass, available electrical power, power consumption, and estimated budget. Users can identify design problems, modify their configurations, and test whether their spacecraft meets mission requirements. Interactive 3D visualization provides a spatial representation of the spacecraft and its configurable components.

ORBITFORGE incorporates NASA mission references and scientific instrument information from missions such as the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) and Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO). These references connect gameplay objectives with real planetary science, including lunar hydrogen mapping, surface imaging, mineral identification, and subsurface investigation.

The application distinguishes referenced scientific information from simplified gameplay assumptions. Mission limits, estimated costs, and certain engineering parameters are illustrative rather than official NASA spacecraft specifications.

The application was developed using React, JavaScript, Vite, CSS, Three.js, React Three Fiber, and React Three Drei. It is deployed as a publicly accessible web application.

ORBITFORGE aims to make space mission planning more understandable through hands-on experimentation. Instead of only reading about spacecraft engineering, users can explore how engineering decisions affect mission feasibility and scientific objectives.

The project combines real mission references, interactive spacecraft configuration, engineering trade-offs, simulation, and 3D visualization into one accessible learning experience.
